program_name: Artificial Intelligence and High Performance Computing Technologies
teaching_language: Fully English-taught (category 1). This is a standalone, complete two-year Master's Degree Programme (Laurea Magistrale) delivered entirely in English - it is NOT an English pathway/curriculum inside an Italian-named degree, and it is NOT an interuniversity/joint degree with another university. Apply@UniTo lists 'Study language: English' and the programme description states: 'All courses are taught in English, fostering an international learning environment.' The programme is run solely by the University of Turin (Department of Computer Science), although it is affiliated with the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking EUMaster4HPC European network (a network/label, not a joint degree). No Italian language requirement is imposed for admission.
campus: Turin (Torino), Italy - Department of Computer Science (Dipartimento di Informatica), University of Turin
degree_class: LM-18 (Classe delle lauree magistrali in Informatica / Computer Science). UNITO internal course code: 0805M21. 120 ECTS, 2 years. [uncertain]
admission_type: Open access / free admission ('accesso libero') postgraduate degree, subject to curricular entry requirements and verification of personal preparation. There is NO numerus clausus (no restricted number of places) for EU/EU-equivalent applicants and no admission ranking test such as TOLC, GRE or SAT. However, a territory quota applies: Apply@UniTo states the degree has 50 available places reserved for non-European applicants residing abroad. Selection is by document assessment against the curricular requirements, plus an oral examination assessing personal preparation (waived if the Bachelor's final grade is at least 95% of the maximum). Applications from international/foreign-qualification candidates are handled through the Apply@UniTo (DreamApply) portal within fixed admission calls. Confirmation that this is an open-access programme: its deadline comes from the 'Fourth admission call for open access postgraduate degree programs only' (25 Aug - 8 Sept 2026), not from the third call which is 'for degree programs with a restricted number of places only'.
application_deadline_eu: 8 September 2026 (23:59:59 CET) - Fourth admission call, open 25 August - 8 September 2026, reserved to Italians, EU citizens, EU-equivalents and non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy. EU applicants could alternatively have applied in the First admission call, 25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026, which was open to all applicants for postgraduate programmes. Academic year 2026/2027.
application_deadline_non_eu: 29 January 2026 (First admission call, open 25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026, open to all applicants including non-EU citizens residing abroad) for academic year 2026/2027. Non-EU applicants residing abroad are NOT eligible for the later 2026 calls (the third, fourth and fifth calls are explicitly reserved to Italians, EU/EU-equivalents and non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy). Non-EU applicants already legally residing in Italy may use the 8 September 2026 fourth-call deadline.
entry_exam_or_test: No written entrance exam, no TOLC, no GRE/GMAT and no SAT. Admission is by assessment of the application dossier against curricular requirements, followed by an ORAL EXAMINATION to assess the candidate's personal preparation. Exemption: candidates whose degree grade is equal to or higher than 95% of the maximum possible grade are exempted from the oral examination. The same oral examination is also used to assess English language proficiency when the applicant does not submit one of the accepted English certificates.
academic_requirements: Entry qualification: a first-cycle diploma (Bachelor's / undergraduate degree) obtained after at least three years of university education, including degrees earned abroad. Specifically: a Bachelor's Degree in Italian class L-31 (Computer Science), or another first-cycle degree recognised as suitable. Minimum grade threshold: final degree grade equal to or exceeding 7/10 of the maximum possible grade (i.e. at least 70% of the maximum mark). Credit requirements: at least 48 ECTS/CFU in the INFO-01/A (Computer Science) and/or IINF-05/A (Computer Engineering) disciplinary sectors, AND at least 18 ECTS/CFU in the MATH (Mathematics) sectors (discrete and continuous mathematics). Adequate university-level background is additionally required in ALL of the following areas: (1) programming according to the main paradigms and languages; (2) computer architectures and operating systems; (3) computer networks and security; (4) databases and knowledge representation; (5) algorithms and data structures; (6) formal languages and compilers; (7) discrete and continuous mathematics. For foreign qualifications, correspondence with the relevant Italian disciplinary sectors is assessed on the basis of course content (syllabus). Personal preparation is verified through an oral examination, waived when the degree grade is at least 95% of the maximum. Places/quota: no restricted number for EU/EU-equivalent applicants (open access); 50 available places are reserved for non-European applicants residing abroad. Duration 2 years / 120 ECTS; students may choose full-time or part-time status each year, with tuition fees varying accordingly.
language_requirements: English: applicants must hold an international certification demonstrating English proficiency at a minimum level of CEFR B2. The certificate must have been obtained no more than three years prior to the application. Accepted certificates and minimum scores: Cambridge Certificate of Proficiency in English (CPE); Cambridge Certificate in Advanced English (CAE); Cambridge First Certificate in English (FCE) with minimum score 173 (Grade B); PTE Academic with minimum score 65; IELTS with minimum overall score 6.0 out of 9 and no component below 6; Trinity College ISE II. EXEMPTION / ALTERNATIVE: if none of the above certifications is provided, English language proficiency will be assessed during the oral examination. Italian: no Italian language requirement is stated for admission, since the programme is taught entirely in English. Note that TOEFL is not named in the official list of accepted certificates on the Apply@UniTo course page.
required_documents: Submitted through the Apply@UniTo (DreamApply) portal. General requirements for postgraduate applicants with a foreign qualification: (1) entry qualification / Bachelor's degree certificate and academic transcript of records (accepted in English, French, Italian or Spanish; if issued in any other language, both the original document and a certified translation must be uploaded); (2) copy of a valid passport / ID document; (3) motivation letter in English or Italian (explicitly required for postgraduate degree programmes); (4) English language certificate at CEFR B2 or above, obtained within the last 3 years (or accept assessment at the oral examination); (5) evidence of the minimum credit requirements (48 ECTS in INFO-01/A and/or IINF-05/A, 18 ECTS in MATH sectors) - typically via transcript; (6) optional but recommended: the degree programme syllabus / course descriptions issued by the foreign institution, with a translation into Italian, English, French or Spanish - used to map foreign courses onto the required Italian disciplinary sectors; (7) payment of the non-refundable EUR 60 application fee within the call deadline (the same amount whether one or two degree programmes are selected). After submission, UNITO may additionally request a Declaration of Value (Dichiarazione di Valore), Statement of Verification or Statement of Comparability issued by CIMEA. At the enrolment stage the International Students Office may request further documents beyond those uploaded at application.

uncertainty_notes: 1) DEGREE CLASS [uncertain]: LM-18 and the UNITO course code 0805M21 could NOT be verified by direct retrieval. www.unito.it, en.unito.it and unito.coursecatalogue.cineca.it all block automated access (HTTP 403 / AWS WAF human-verification page), and the programme microsite www.aihpc.unito.it refuses connections at network level (ECONNREFUSED on 130.186.3.24:443) and has no Wayback Machine snapshot (HTTP 404 from web.archive.org). LM-18 therefore rests on two independent search-engine index snippets of the official www.unito.it course page, which agree with each other and are consistent with the L-31 entry requirement and the Department of Computer Science. Apply@UniTo does not publish the degree class (its 'code' field is null and 'awards' are empty). LM-18 should be re-verified against the official Regolamento Didattico when the microsite becomes reachable. 2) BRAND-NEW PROGRAMME: this is a new degree launching in academic year 2026/27, so it does not yet appear consistently across all UNITO portal pages; the richest and most authoritative reachable source is the Apply@UniTo (DreamApply) course record, last updated 2026-06-23. 3) DISCIPLINARY SECTOR CODE DISCREPANCY: Apply@UniTo writes the required sectors as 'INFO-01/A' and 'IINF-05/A' (the new Italian sector codes introduced in 2024), while search-indexed Italian text of the www.unito.it page renders them as 'INF-01/A' and 'INF-05/A'. These refer to the same Computer Science / Computer Engineering sectors; the Apply@UniTo spelling has been used here. Similarly the mathematics requirement is written as 'MATH (Mathematics) sectors' on Apply@UniTo and as 'discrete and continuous mathematics' areas on the Italian page. 4) NON-EU DEADLINE ALREADY PASSED: the only 2026/27 window open to non-EU applicants residing abroad was 25 Nov 2025 - 29 Jan 2026; as of the research date (1 September 2026) only the EU / Italy-resident call (closing 8 Sept 2026) is still open. Prospective non-EU applicants abroad should expect an equivalent first call around November 2026 - January 2027 for a.y. 2027/28, but that calendar is not yet published. 5) TOEFL is not listed among the accepted English certificates on the official Apply@UniTo page; whether TOEFL is nevertheless accepted in practice is unverified. 6) The '50 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad' is a territory quota, not a numerus clausus - the programme is otherwise open access; no ranking/entrance test is used to allocate these places beyond the standard requirement check and oral exam, per the sources reachable. 7) EUMaster4HPC / EuroHPC JU network affiliation was reported in search-indexed material but could not be confirmed on a directly retrievable official unito.it page; it is a network affiliation and does not make this a joint/interuniversity degree.
